findings.message: Change 108 adds a module (modules/git-accounts) but also edits platform code. It changes a platform migration (0033 on auth.git_identity), packages/auth/src/git-identity.ts (linkGitIdentity behaviour, setGitHubIdentities, gitIdentitiesOf), packages/core/src/env.ts, packages/core/src/secrets/connectors.ts, packages/ai/src/scripted-writes.ts, apps/web/components/chat/Chat.tsx and apps/web/lib/chat-outcome.ts (a new `open` card outcome), and adds an app route. docs/module-standard.md says a module change touches only modules/<name>/ plus one CODEOWNERS line. Fix: move the platform pieces (the auth schema and identity functions, the env vars, the connector entry, the chat-card `open` outcome, the callback route) into a platform-lane change that this module depends on. Or record a product-owner exemption in change.md. The size waiver covers splitting the module, not the lane rule.
findings.scenario: modules/git-accounts change diff → also writes packages/db/migrations/0033, packages/auth/src/git-identity.ts and apps/web/components/chat/Chat.tsx, which the module standard forbids for a module change

findings.message: readGitHubUser makes three fetch calls to GitHub with no timeout or AbortSignal. completeConnect runs them inside its defineService transaction, after it has locked the connect_state row with UPDATE. A slow or hung GitHub keeps a Postgres transaction and a pooled connection open with no limit, and the callback request never returns. Fix: give each fetch a timeout (AbortSignal.timeout). Better, read GitHub before the write transaction and pass the result into the service, so no network call runs inside the transaction.
findings.scenario: GitHub /user/emails stalls → the callback request hangs, its transaction holds a pool connection and the connect_state row lock with no limit; a few such requests exhaust the pool for the whole app

findings.message: setGitHubIdentities checks which emails other people hold, then inserts with `on conflict do nothing`, and returns `linked: kept` without looking at what the inserts did. If another writer links the same email between the check and the insert, the unique index git_identity_email makes the insert a silent no-op. The person is still told the email was linked, and the audit row and connected event count it. Fix: add `returning email` to each insert and build `linked` from the rows actually inserted; report the rest as skipped. Add a test with two real concurrent writers (B7).
findings.scenario: An Admin accepts a delivery.git-identity suggestion linking kasun@lumenlabs.test to Nimal while Kasun's connect is between its check and its insert → Kasun's insert does nothing; the callback says "@kasun-dias, 2 emails" and the audit says 2 emails, but only 1 row is stored

findings.message: Before 0033, auth.git_identity was unique only on (tenant_id, provider, login), compared case-sensitively. Data that rule allowed now breaks the new unique indexes: two logins with the same email (for example two delivery link suggestions accepted for one person), or logins that differ only in case. On such data `create unique index` fails, and the deploy's migration stops. Fix: before creating the indexes, de-duplicate or merge the clashing rows, keeping the oldest and recording what was dropped. Add a migration test seeded with those duplicates.
findings.scenario: An existing tenant has rows (github, 'kd', 'k@x.test') and (github, 'kasun-old', 'k@x.test'), both linked from delivery suggestions → `create unique index git_identity_email` raises a unique violation → the migration aborts and the app won't start

findings.message: The GitHub accounts card is pinned to get_secret_meta {connector:'github-oauth'}. That tool throws not found when the credential doesn't exist, which is exactly when the card says "Not configured" and shows its Ask button with the same pin. So the pin doesn't resolve to the status the card shows, and R3 counts a pin with no matching read as missing. Fix: pin a read that answers in both states, for example get_my_git_identities (it returns `configured`) or a connector-status read that returns 'not configured' instead of throwing.
findings.scenario: A tenant with no github-oauth credential → an Admin opens Settings › Integrations and pins the GitHub accounts card or clicks Ask amax → resolving the pin calls get_secret_meta and fails with 'credential github-oauth not found'

findings.message: myGitAccounts assumes one GitHub login per person and only email-bearing rows. It takes `login` from mine[0] and lists every email row under it, and it drops rows with a null email. A person can hold several GitHub logins, or a login-only row, linked earlier through delivery link suggestions. The screen then shows the wrong login, myIdentity returns emails under the wrong login, and the red Disconnect card says "@a and N emails" while disconnectGitHub deletes every provider='github' row, including the other logins and the login-only rows. Fix: group by login in the read model, and have the disconnect card name every login and row that the delete will remove (or scope the delete to what the card lists).
findings.scenario: Kasun has rows (kasun-dias, k@x) and (kasun-old, null) from an accepted suggestion → the page says 'Connected as @kasun-dias', the card says 'Disconnect GitHub: @kasun-dias and 1 email' → confirming deletes 2 rows, including @kasun-old, which the card never named

findings.message: When AMAX_BASE_URL is unset, redirectUri falls back to http://localhost:3000. A production deployment without it issues authorize links whose redirect_uri is localhost, and does not flag the missing config. Fix: when the base URL is missing, refuse connect_github with a setup error (fail closed), or derive the URL from the request in the callback/issue path. Don't use a hard-coded localhost.
findings.scenario: A prod deployment without AMAX_BASE_URL → connect_github returns a GitHub link with redirect_uri=http://localhost:3000/api/git/github/callback → GitHub rejects it with a redirect_uri mismatch, or sends the person to localhost

findings.message: The callback copies `error_description` from the query string, and any exception's message, into `reason`. The Git accounts page then shows that text in a trusted status line. React escapes it, so it isn't XSS, but anyone can make a link that shows chosen text on amax's page, and internal error messages (database or authorization text) reach the user. Fix: map error codes to fixed messages, show only known, safe error messages from completeConnect, and log the rest.
findings.scenario: /api/git/github/callback?error=x&error_description=Your+account+is+locked,+call+0123 → the page shows "GitHub wasn't connected: Your account is locked, call 0123"

findings.message: The Postgres array literal is built by joining emails into `{"a","b"}` without escaping `"` or `\`. The value is bound as a parameter, so this isn't SQL injection, but a legal email with a quoted local part breaks the literal or splits it wrongly. Fix: pass a real array parameter (sql`= any(${emails})` with an array bind, or sql.join).
findings.scenario: GitHub lists the verified email "a\"b"@x.test → '{""a"b"@x.test"}'::text[] fails to parse → the whole connect errors

findings.message: connect_state rows, used or expired, are never removed, so the table grows with every connect attempt. Fix: delete used and expired rows in completeConnect or issueConnect (for example, rows older than 10 minutes for the same user).
findings.scenario: Every connect attempt → a row that stays forever

findings.message: AC-1 says GITHUB_CLIENT_ID and GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET environment variables configure GitHub. The code (and the module standard: no credentials in env) uses the 031 credential `github-oauth` instead. Update AC-1 to match. AC-10 also says suggestions are closed 'for an email', but the code withdraws by the target `github:<login>`.

withdrawSuggestions runs under the job context 'git-accounts.connect', so the dismissed suggestions record the job as their decider, not the person who connected. It also commits in its own transaction before the outer write commits. Fix: run it as the person's context (or record actsFor), so the record says who did it.
findings.scenario: Kasun connects → agents.suggestion.decided_by is the job 'git-accounts.connect', not Kasun

findings.message: The Disconnect card promises 'proposals you already own keep you as owner', but nothing keeps that true. Delivery's sync works out the owner again from the repo on every run (`repoOwnerStale` → `ownerFromRepo` in modules/delivery/server/owner.ts:52). Once the verified identity is deleted, the next sync sets the owner to null for any proposal whose author email matched only through it. The same thing happens on reconnect, which drops emails GitHub no longer lists (setGitHubIdentities `removed`). Fix: either keep owners that came from a verified identity (for example, sync never clears an owner that was set from one), or change the card and README to say ownership is lost at the next sync. Add a test: connect, sync, disconnect, sync, owner unchanged.
findings.scenario: Kasun connects GitHub with 4821937+kasun-dias@users.noreply.github.com → the sync makes Kasun owner of FLT-541 (as in the owner-091 108 test) → Kasun confirms Disconnect, where the card says the owner is kept → the next sync finds no match for the no-reply email → FLT-541's owner becomes null (Unassigned).

findings.message: GitHub's replies are never checked against a schema. `String(user.login)` and `Number(user.id)` turn a missing field into the login 'undefined' and NaN. A /user/emails body that isn't an array throws a TypeError, which the callback then shows the person as its message. Fix: parse both bodies with zod (login a non-empty string, id an integer, emails an array of {email, verified}) and refuse when they don't match.
findings.scenario: /user returns 200 `{}` (an API change or a proxy page) → setGitHubIdentities stores verified identities under the login 'undefined' and reports '@undefined connected'.

findings.message: unlinkIdentity and disconnectGitHub run raw `delete from auth.git_identity` from module code. @amax/auth already owns writes to that table (`unlinkGitIdentity`, which delivery's suggestion undo uses). That makes two copies of the auth-schema write, and they can drift. Delete through auth's helpers (add a by-user variant for disconnect).

The full authorize URL, single-use state included, goes back as the tool result. It ends up in the chat transcript, the trace and the model's context, while the README says only the state's hash is kept. Treat the URL like `reveal`: show it on the card only and keep it out of the conversation and the trace.
